content:
We have list of functional groups. Our target reaction: chalcone (aryl-CO-CH=CH-aryl) cyclizes to flavanone (benzopyran). The forward reaction: intramolecular Michael addition forming C-C bond (between carbonyl alpha carbon (enolate) and beta carbon) and forming C-O bond (forming heterocycle) while breaking C-O carbonyl? Actually carbonyl oxygen becomes part of ether (C-O bond). So functional groups formed: ether oxygens. Broken: ketones (carbonyl) and aromatic hydroxyls? Wait chalcone has phenolic OH? In flavanone formation, the phenolic OH may be present? The description says aromatic hydroxyls are broken. So the starting chalcone may have phenol that becomes part of ether? Actually flavanone formation often from 2'-hydroxychalcone (i.e., ortho-hydroxy). The phenolic OH attacks carbonyl after enolate formation, forming heterocycle, breaking O-H bond (hydroxyl). So aromatic hydroxyl broken.

Thus functional groups broken: ketones, aromatic hydroxyls. Formed: ether oxygens.

Our earlier search with those functional groups returned empty. Maybe need also include "C-C bonds formed"? The functional groups list includes "C-C double bonds", "C-C triple bonds". Not bond formation. For bonds, we can specify bonds_formed: "6-6" (aryl-aryl) and "6-8" (aryl-oxygen). But earlier search gave empty.

Maybe the template ID is known? Could be a known template for intramolecular Michael addition forming flavanone. Could search by criteria without functional groups broken? Let's try search with only functional_groups_formed: ["ether oxygens"] and maybe bonds_formed.
